abstract.t: Agentic systems can authenticate successfully, hold a valid authorization object, and still be unsafe to execute because required evidence is missing, the software has not reached a required assurance stage, the authority epoch is stale, a prior revocation is unresolved, or a human-approval requirement is unsatisfied. This document defines the High-Assurance Agent Control Envelope (HAACE), a protocol-neutral profile that binds an exact agent action to identity status, authorization state, policy, assurance stage, evidence state, authority epoch, revocation state, oversight requirements, and an action-time decision. HAACE requires fail-closed treatment of missing or indeterminate prerequisites, separates authorization from execution, and produces non-bearer decision and execution receipts.
